opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ian Johnson (employee ID E028) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E028.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Ian Johnson (E028) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Requested admin; recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ian Johnson (E028) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin, so maximum is read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: the HR note lists Ian Johnson as full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by that role), while the Security note lists him as a contractor with basic security training, whose maximum is read and who can never have admin. The employee requested admin, which exceeds the contractor maximum. Given the unresolved conflict on the decisive fact, I grant the most restrictive permissible level consistent with the security record: read.

Which is correct? The access policy is the maximum level. The decision: requested admin. If full-time Payroll Specialist, admin at or below max -> grant admin. If contractor basic -> max read -> grant read.
